speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether a volunteer under the Appropriate Adult Scheme for Young Suspects was present during CNB’s interviews with Justin Lee.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether law enforcement agencies will review their protocols and implementation measures for dealing with crime suspects who are minors or who may have special needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: CNB officers did test buys of the drugs from him, twice, to verify that he was, in fact, selling the drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He was cooperative during his arrest and did not put up any struggle.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: CNB officers were not aware of any issues with Justin’s mental health when he was arrested.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: His mother, Ms Cecilia Ow, was present when Justin was escorted back to his house on 3 February for a follow-up anti-drug operation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Appropriate Adult Scheme for Young Suspects is used for suspects under the age of 16.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The scheme, together with the age limit, had been announced publicly in January 2017.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It was also discussed in Parliament in March 2017, where the age limit was made clear.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, the interviews CNB officers had with Justin were video recorded because of the seriousness of the drug trafficking offence he was being investigated for.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The video recordings have been shown to his mother, Ms Cecilia Ow, on 22 October 2021.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We should add that there is also a separate Appropriate Adults Scheme for Persons with Mental Disabilities, in short, AAPMD.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Justin answered questions without any signs of distress and did not appear to be in need of any assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Justin was composed and coherent, able to logically articulate the flow of events, including sharing about his research on drugs and his trafficking modus operandi.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The IO assessed that he did not need to stop the interview to bring in an Appropriate Adult under the AAPMD Scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, as stated, the interviews were video recorded.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Justin was released on bail on 4 February after about a day in custody.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: His mother came to meet him and brought him back.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Justin was charged on 23 June for drug trafficking offences under the Misuse of Drugs Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He was released on bail on the same day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The next day, on 24 June, Justin was charged in Court.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Prosecution was ready to take the plea.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He did so a total of four times, so the case kept getting postponed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Throughout this period, Justin was out on bail and, as far as CNB is aware, he was at home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He fell to his death near his home on 16 September.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This would indicate that he had taken these drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But this cannot be stated with finality and is subject to the Coroner’s findings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I have looked at this case and asked: why did this young person fall to his death when he was out on bail and was staying at home?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Thirty-two weeks, or about eight months, after he was arrested and released?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The young man could have had a far better future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The question is: how can we bring across to more of our young people the danger of drugs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: How can we also bring across to them and their families, that even if they are arrested, they will still have opportunities to reform and the agencies will help them give up drug-taking and that there can be a good future ahead?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have been putting out this message quite a lot and will have to continue to do so, so that parents and persons who are arrested understand the process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: You have done wrong, but that does not have to be the final word.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Our system is designed to give second chances to help you rehabilitate.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We changed our laws on dealing with pure drug abusers, to not treat them as criminals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Instead, we focus on getting them to change the drug habit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In Justin’s case, he was trafficking drugs and seems like he was also abusing drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But with the right help, he could also have changed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And our processes are structured to provide that guidance and help, after he is dealt with in Court.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We bring in the family into these efforts as well because, without adequate family support, it is difficult to help the young person.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The young man had a lawyer, he was living with his family and the case was set to proceed in Court.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And after the hearing, if he was found guilty, he would then, normally, be put on a path to help him change, rehabilitate himself, as we have said earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: CNB had also made every possible facilitation for him.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Usually, suspects charged with drug-trafficking offences will not be released on bail due to the high flight risk.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, in view of Justin’s age, CNB released him on bail after serving the charges to him on 23 June and allowed him to report to Court the next day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, what made him jump to his death on 16 September, when he was staying at home?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have said, this was some eight months after he had been arrested and released.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He had been charged and the case was fixed for hearing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Is it the fact that the case was coming on in seven days’ time?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Did he speak with anyone about the oncoming case and his concerns?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: How did he have traces of drugs in his blood?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: How is it that he appears to have consumed drugs before his fall?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are many questions and it is difficult to do more than conjecture what the answers are.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I will now deal with the questions that have been asked.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The questions relate to law enforcement agencies’ protocols when conducting investigations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked if we plan to review our protocols for dealing with young suspects and suspects with special needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are regular reviews to ensure that they are up to date.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Ms Denise Phua, in 2016, and Ms Sylvia Lim, in 2017, had asked if all persons under 18 can be supported with an Appropriate Adult during interviews.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Given that the AAYS scheme applies to all persons under 16, the point really is whether it can be extended to persons who are 16 and 17.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We have told both of them that this would be reviewed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There were some difficulties in expanding the scheme to suspects in this age group.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked about CNB’s protocols when conducting drug-related investigations involving young persons with a history of medical or mental health condition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If it is made known to the officers that the subject has medical or mental health conditions and would require special attention, prior to bringing the person in to assist in the investigation, CNB officers will contact the parents or school first, if operationally feasible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Under these circumstances, they will activate an Appropriate Adult to be present during the interview.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If the subject displays any medical or special needs during the interview, officers will pause the investigation and activate support measures, such as activating an Appropriate Adult or sending the person to the Institute of Mental Health for assessment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: CNB will also obtain medical reports to assess if the subject is mentally fit for prosecution.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If the person is observed to be capable of being interviewed, the officers will carry on with the interview.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The point is that they will use their discretion, based on their observations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked for statistics on persons under the age of 18 arrested who had a history of mental health conditions, and those who, subsequently, were hospitalised or passed away.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is also not meaningful for us to track it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These individuals may have passed away or been hospitalised due to varying reasons not related to the investigations, such as inherent health problems or injuries sustained by themselves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Justin’s case falls in the small minority of 16%, because he was openly trafficking.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The general approach when dealing with young suspects is to, where possible, avoid criminalising their conduct, give them a second chance and help them in their rehabilitation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Suitable youths who have been arrested for minor offences can be referred to diversionary programmes, such as the Guidance Programme introduced in 1997, which has a strong focus on counselling and rehabilitation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Placing youth offenders on diversionary programmes allows them to be accountable for their actions and prevents disruption in other areas of development, such as education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Justin will also have been placed on such processes, after sentencing, if he had been found guilty.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah asked how law enforcement agencies identify vulnerable persons and persons with mental disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Training is given to our officers in this respect.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Home Team has also worked with the Agency for Integrated Care to increase officers’ awareness of mental health conditions and help them to identify and respond to persons observed to have some mental health issues.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In gist, the officer will check if the person has a Developmental Disability Registry Identity Card issued by the National Council of Social Service (NCSS), look out for information that the person may be undergoing treatment at healthcare institutions for diagnosed mental disabilities and observe the behavioural traits of the person.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah also asked how family members of a young person, whose death is suspected to be related to the person’s interaction with the criminal justice system, can request for a formal investigation into the death.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: First, the person may have been in official custody of a law enforcement agency at the time of death.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Second, the person may be undergoing investigation and passed away subsequently due to suicide, while not in custody.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Police are required to report their findings to the Coroner, who is a judicial officer appointed under the State Courts Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the first scenario, a Coroner’s Inquiry must be held to determine the cause of and circumstances connected with the death.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the second scenario, it is not mandatory to hold a Coroner’s Inquiry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: However, the Coroner may still decide to hold an inquiry, after considering other factors, including the desire of any member of the deceased’s immediate family to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He was in custody for investigation for about a day in February.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Since his release on 4 February, he had been staying at his home, except for the one day in June when he reported to CNB and was charged in Court.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Member does not appear to be aware of previous announcements and discussions on the scheme.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I also thank the Minister of State for the clarifications and explanations.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Just recently, we heard about six officers who were injured in the line of duty – and those are only the reported cases.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the fight against drug abuse, I think CNB officers face similar and more serious perils as well.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How are our CNB officers trained to handle young suspects and persons with mental disabilities and, at the same time, balance that training so that it would not compromise the operational effectiveness and also their safety?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, CNB officers have to deal with various situations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The profile of the people that they deal with also vary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As such, it is important for them to be well-equipped not only from the socio-emotional perspective but also to have the skills to go on the operation as well as to engage the public with regard to preventive drug education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And I am appreciative of the Member recognising that their job requires the skills and training and, as such, it is something that they place their emphasis on, not only as part of the job scope but also about protecting Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I interact regularly with CNB officers and one thing I am proud of them for is that they are very clear about their commitment and passion in protecting Singapore, to ensure that the harms of drugs do not penetrate or affect the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This is something that I feel very proud of our CNB officers for.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And CNB equips its officers with the skills to handle their jobs through various structured and customised training programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, in some parts of the training, where they learn about conducting video-recorded interviews, trainers will also revise the Appropriate Adult schemes and provide relevant case studies so that they are able to relate to and be familiar with the situations which warrant the activation of the scheme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, essentially, they are trained and they get refreshed and they share case studies together because every case is different.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I hope I have answered the Member's question.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, the Minister of State made extensive comments about the case of Justin Lee.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Justin Lee was my resident and I would like to clarify that I understand from his family that the Coroner's findings into his death have not been issued yet.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Therefore, I am reserving any questions that I may have until after the findings have been issued.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Earlier, the Minister of State specifically mentioned the Appropriate Adult Scheme and that the cut-off age of 16 years had been announced in 2017, so, everyone should be clear about that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But at the same time, I think he will acknowledge that in 2019, we did have a change in our CYPA, the Children and Young Persons Act.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We amended the definition of "child" to extend the cut-off age to 18.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We can understand that it may need to be phased in and so on but, at the very least, does the Ministry not agree that we must commit to moving all these protections, whether legal or procedural, to the cut-off age of 18, in line with the amendment to the CYPA on the definition of "child"?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For special needs suspects, the Minister of State mentioned that there are Appropriate Adults also available to help vulnerable adults.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We take note of the Member's view on the CYPA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I want to assure the Member this is something that we have also been looking at and we also want to make sure we facilitate this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, as I have shared with the House earlier, there are constraints that we are facing with regard to the Appropriate Adult Scheme because essentially, the Appropriate Adults are volunteers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will need more volunteers to support the expansion to cover more young suspects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In order for them to come on board, we need to train them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We also need to provide face-to-face training to ensure that the volunteers are well-equipped to perform their roles.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: During this current pandemic, there are constraints on conducting face-to-face training due to the safe distancing measures.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Hence, it is not easy to ramp up the pool of Appropriate Adults quickly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If this age limit is further increased to 21, this would be even more significant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Without a sufficient pool of Appropriate Adults, interviews will be delayed until an Appropriate Adult is available.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This could add more strain on the person who is being investigated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the second question, I would like to share with Ms Sylvia Lim that we take every investigation seriously.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We train our officers to better understand the behavioural component, the needs of the suspect, as well as how we can facilitate the interviews, all in the name of doing it fairly and professionally.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, if there is a need for us to reach out to the family members, we will do so.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Throughout the investigation in February, did the Police offer to activate the Appropriate Adult Scheme for the mentally-challenged?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Or is it incumbent in our system that the suspect should ask for it and the Police do not volunteer it?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I have shared earlier, we want to be fair and professional in how we deal with the suspects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will observe, we will find all ways we can, to see if there is a need for support.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it is not that the person has to declare or has to ask for it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to make sure that the person has a fair process, as part of the investigation.
